history.period: Claimed 5,000 years old (traditional, unverified); rediscovered 1962, opened to the public 1966
history.summary: Rock-cut cave Shiva temple near Ziro, dedicated to Lord Lakulisha, described in tradition as the 28th incarnation of Lord Shiva in the 28th Kali Yuga of the seventh Manvantara. Cave walls carry Sanskrit inscriptions (the Kalika Purana is cited locally) with stalactites and stalagmites inside; it sits about 300 ft up a hill and is reached by a flight of steps. The 5,000-year age claim is traditional and unverified; discovery in 1962 (public opening 1966) is consistently reported. Location conflict: most sources list it under Ziro, but one government eco-heritage page calls it a Daporijo (Upper Subansiri) destination - town kept as Ziro per CSV, flagged. No geocoder POI match; coordinates are Ziro town-level (approximate).

name: Meghna Cave Temple
town_description: Ziro is a plateau town in Lower Subansiri district, heartland of the Apatani tribe famed for its wet-rice cultivation, pine hills and bamboo groves. One of Arunachal's oldest towns and a UNESCO World Heritage tentative site, it hosts the annual Ziro Festival of Music and is a base for exploring Talley Valley and nearby temples.

travel.airport: Donyi Polo Airport (Hollongi/Itanagar), about 100 km away (4-hr drive); Lilabari (Assam) about 123 km
travel.railway: Naharlagun railway station, about 100 km away
travel.road: Ziro is about 167 km from Itanagar by road (NH-13); local taxis/transport from Ziro town to the cave
